# REFERENCES — sources of truth

When implementing a mechanic, **consult all three tiers in order**. Disagreements are normal; document them in `docs/known_divergences.md` and pick the source that matches our goal (PS-compatibility, since mimikyu is trained on PS replays).

## Tier 1 — Pokémon Showdown (`smogon/pokemon-showdown`)

**The compatibility oracle.** This is what mimikyu's replay corpus was generated by, so PS-matching behavior is the definition of "correct" for us.

- Repo: https://github.com/smogon/pokemon-showdown
- Key paths:
  - `data/moves.ts` — move definitions, all gens (gen-9 file is current; older gens via `data/mods/genN/moves.ts` deltas)
  - `data/abilities.ts` — same pattern
  - `data/items.ts` — same pattern
  - `data/mods/champions/` — **Champions VGC overlay** (sig moves, etc. — see mimikyu's `reference_champions_vgc_mod_data.md`)
  - `sim/battle.ts`, `sim/pokemon.ts`, `sim/side.ts` — the actual game-state machine
  - `sim/SIM-PROTOCOL.md` — protocol spec (we emit a compatible subset)
- Strengths: ground truth for what mimikyu has seen; actively maintained; covers gens 1–9 + LGPE + every official format.
- Weaknesses: event-driven JS, hard to read mechanic-in-isolation; the same move's behavior is spread across handler callbacks; long-tail edge cases buried in test files.

## Tier 2 — pkmn/engine (`pkmn/engine`)

**Design template + chance-aware mechanic spec.** Reading pkmn/engine's `mechanics.zig` is the fastest way to understand what's actually load-bearing in a mechanic vs. what's PS engine cruft.

- Repo: https://github.com/pkmn/engine
- Key paths:
  - `docs/DESIGN.md` — read first, before writing any Rust
  - `docs/NOTES.md` — scheibo's 23-step "adding a generation" playbook (we don't follow it but it lists what we need to think about)
  - `src/lib/gen1/data.zig` — bit-packed Pokémon struct, gold standard
  - `src/lib/gen1/mechanics.zig` — the move/effect dispatcher (currently the most polished reference)
  - `src/lib/gen1/chance.zig` — MCTS-ready outcome enumeration
  - `src/lib/gen2/` — partial, lots of `==TODO==` in README; useful as "what changed in gen 2" diff
- Strengths: data-oriented, instrumented for search, design philosophy explicitly written down.
- Weaknesses: only gens 1–2; one maintainer; "no shared code between gens" is the opposite of our approach.

## Tier 3 — Bulbapedia + Smogon /research/

**Mechanic explainers when the code is opaque.** When PS or pkmn/engine implementation is too dense to read directly, these tell you what the mechanic *means*.

- Bulbapedia: https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net (search "Damage", "Critical hit", "Speed tie", "Tera Type", etc.)
- Smogon /research/ subforum: https://www.smogon.com/forums/forums/past-generations-research.213/ — mechanic deep-dives, especially gen-1/2 oddities
- Bulbapedia is canonical for the *cartridge*; PS is canonical for the *simulator*. We follow PS where they disagree (replay corpus alignment).

## Cross-references

- mimikyu's `localdex` (`~/Dev/localdex`) is a TypeScript dump of `@pkmn/dex` we already use; the same JSON dumps drive vgc-engine's `build.rs`.
- mimikyu's `data/ps_data/*.json` is the post-OCR slug dicts; useful as a sanity check against `@pkmn/dex` IDs.
- mimikyu's `reference_champions_vgc_mod_data.md` documents the Champions overlay we replicate in vgc-engine's mod registration.

## Tools

- `gh` CLI for browsing PS / pkmn/engine source without local clones (the agents do this; humans should `git clone --depth 1` locally for grep speed).
- Don't fetch full PS history — `--depth 1` is enough.
